ASEAN-SCOPE-2026.claim: ASEAN SCOPE Trade published current cross-border MSME evidence using a survey of business support organisations representing over 220,000 businesses and 30 private-sector/BSO consultations; aggregate friction is not itself evidence of an unowned transaction layer.

OECD-ASEAN-2026.claim: OECD 2026 reports substantial divergence and growing heterogeneity in ASEAN domestic digital-trade regulation; this is upstream context, not a specific paid need or accessible permission rail.

HKTDC-ASEAN-2026.claim: A Q1 2026 HKTDC survey of Hong Kong traders found compliance a leading concern for respondents active in ASEAN e-commerce and third-party platforms a major preferred route; findings must not be generalized to all ASEAN firms.

TIKTOK-BRAND-MY-20260427.claim: TikTok Shop Malaysia has a live brand qualification pathway with documented owner/direct and multilayer authorized reseller states; it controls qualification within its marketplace, not a general public cross-platform dealer-authority registry.

GS1MY-PRODUCT-2026.claim: GS1 Verified by GS1 authenticates product identifier and basic brand-owned product attributes; it does not by itself attest that a given off-platform counterparty has a current territory-specific distribution grant.

PENANG-INSTITUTE-20260331.claim: Penang Institute March 2026 analysis identifies federal-health/state-social-service handoff fragmentation and reports a stakeholder perception gap; its proposed state-led coordinating body is a proposal, not evidence of accessible private data rights or independent budget.

HOMAGE-PENANG.claim: Homage currently sells Penang post-discharge/home nursing and personal care, provides in-person assessment/care plans and matches trained professionals; incumbent private care matching exists but does not establish a government cross-agency integration rail.

ASEAN-ATR-ASSIST.claim: ASEAN has existing trade repositories and the ASSIST public operational-trade complaint path; these are not blanket solutions to marketplace access but prevent relabeling public guidance/remedy as independent operator-owned control.

MATRade-EBIZLINK-20260212.claim: MATRADE reports its eBizLink export digitalization programme benefited 1,855 Malaysian companies across 37 activities in 2023–25; business-support action rails are already active, although coverage of all firms is not implied.

examined_formations.title: Regional small importer evaluating an off-platform branded-goods offer -> independently check counterparty territory-specific reseller authority before purchase
examined_formations.observed_partial_flow: TikTok marketplace sellers upload tiered brand authorization evidence while GS1 separately validates product identity; neither proves a generic portable third-party authorization attestation outside that platform.
competing_outcome_hypotheses: Portable distributor-authority verification before off-platform first order
Existing brand-direct confirmation and channel-specific authorization may already suffice without a neutral intermediary
material_contradictions: Product authenticity is not seller authority
The brand controls permission and revocation; its callable verification surface is not publicly established
Regional aggregate compliance friction is not observed repeated paid demand for authority checking

examined_formations.title: Penang family transitioning from hospital discharge to continued non-clinical/clinical home support -> family-to-care-service matching
examined_formations.observed_partial_flow: Penang Institute documents families carrying handoff information across health/social institutions; private Homage already assesses needs and matches care providers for post-discharge care in Penang.
competing_outcome_hypotheses: Federal-to-state welfare eligibility and records integration
material_contradictions: Private care matching already exists and is not equivalent to state care integration
Institutional interoperability needs state/federal data authority and trained clinical judgment; no callable private gate or independent payer was found

examined_formations.title: Already-exporting ASEAN microbusiness encounters a new destination marketplace eligibility/compliance gate -> market-entry access and transaction continuity
examined_formations.observed_partial_flow: Active sellers use established marketplaces, export BSOs, government information/remedy resources and country-specific compliance providers, but still face heterogeneous market rules.
competing_outcome_hypotheses: Local legal/registration or licensed fulfillment access to an otherwise blocked channel
material_contradictions: Policy fragmentation is documented but lacks a source-bound named affected transaction unit and publicly callable independent gate
Only a marketplace can grant its account access; only competent authorities decide regulated compliance; MATRADE and BSOs already operate adjacent support
